title: Per-model latency SLOs and alerting policy (perf canary) v1
author: Aisha Bello
body:
## Purpose
This page sets Redwood’s alerting policy for **per-model performance regressions** found by the production **perf-canary**. It translates canary signals into SRE concepts (SLOs, error budgets, paging hygiene), defines **warning vs paging** thresholds, and records **routing and ownership**.

It is an internal policy, not a customer-facing SLA. Its job is to protect serving performance while keeping on-call load reasonable.

## Scope
In scope:
- Perf-canary synthetic measurements per model (optionally per region/tier/SKU).
- Alerts on **p95 latency regressions** and **tokens/sec drops**, with queueing vs runtime-execution breakouts.
- Routing to #eng-runtime, #eng-oncall, and incident-bot.

Out of scope:
- Shadowing customer prompts or any alerting on customer content.
- Quality regressions (Applied ML / eval harness).

## Key concepts
### “SLO” in this context
Perf regressions are handled as an **SLO-like reliability signal**. Canary traffic is synthetic and small, so it is a **leading indicator** rather than a direct measure of customer experience.

Two tiers follow from that:
- **Warning alerts**: actionable, non-paging, for early drift and quick triage.
- **Paging alerts**: for sustained, high-confidence regressions on **top models** or broad infra/runtime events.

### Primary signals
Alerts compare against a stored baseline keyed on:
- model + model_version
- runtime_build_id
- hardware_sku
- region (optional, when variance differs by region)

Primary regressions:
- **Latency**: p95 end-to-end latency (ms), plus runtime-only p95 where available
- **Throughput**: tokens/sec

Triage signals (dashboards and incident context only): queueing time p95, prefill p95, decode p95, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate.

## Ownership and responsibilities
- **Primary owner: Serving Runtime** — kernel/scheduler regressions, runtime builds, canary-service correctness.
  - Tech lead: Noah Patel
  - Kernel escalation: Hiro Tanaka
  - Scheduling escalation: Sofia Ivanova
- **SRE owner: SRE** — alerting policy, paging hygiene, on-call readiness, incident workflow.
  - SRE sponsor: Sean Gallagher
  - Routing/incident hygiene: Rafael Mendes
- **Platform Telemetry** — metrics pipeline latency/availability and label cardinality.
  - Lead: Logan Wright

### Expectations
- Runtime acknowledges warnings (Slack reaction or reply) within business hours.
- SRE primary on-call actively manages paging incidents, pulling in runtime as needed.
- Baseline-affecting changes (kernel selection, batching heuristics, SKU swaps, region migrations) are announced per the change-management section.

## Alert tiers and policy
### Tier 0: Informational
For new models/regions during ramp-up: dashboards only, no Slack alerts, used to characterize variance and pick thresholds.

### Tier 1: Warning (non-paging)
Routing: incident-bot posts to **#eng-runtime** (threaded, deduped), mentioning @runtime-perf-canary only.

Policy: requires minimum sample size and a sustained window; includes dashboard links, baseline vs observed, and an attribution hint.

Default warning triggers (per model tuple, overridable):
- p95 end-to-end latency: **>= +10%** vs baseline for **15 minutes**
- tokens/sec: **<= -8%** vs baseline for **15 minutes**
- runtime-only p95 latency (if available): **>= +10%** vs baseline for **15 minutes**

If a model's warnings are noisy, tune its per-model thresholds instead of disabling globally.

### Tier 2: Paging (Sev2)
Routing:
- Page **#eng-oncall** via incident-bot (Sev2).
- Incident thread auto-created in **#incidents** with the runbook link.
- Runtime is mentioned in the thread, not paged unless escalation criteria are met.

Eligibility (any one): **Top Model**; regression across **multiple models** pointing at infra/runtime; active rollout gate.

Default paging triggers:
- Top model p95 latency: **>= +25%** vs baseline for **30 minutes**
- Top model tokens/sec: **<= -15%** vs baseline for **30 minutes**
- Multi-model event: **>= 3 models** in warning sharing a dimension (region+SKU or runtime_build_id) for **20 minutes**

### Tier 3: Paging (Sev1) — rare
Routing: page #eng-oncall (Sev1) and engage runtime on-call immediately.

Default Sev1 triggers:
- Top model p95 latency: **>= +35%** vs baseline for **20 minutes** and worsening
- tokens/sec: **<= -25%** vs baseline for **20 minutes** on top model(s)
- Outage-like performance event across regions or most top models

## Model criticality
- **Top model**: high traffic and/or enterprise-critical; paging once tuned.
- **High-risk model**: newly onboarded or recently changed kernel/scheduler/fleet; warnings early, paging later.
- **Standard**: warnings only unless part of a multi-model event.

The list is kept in control-plane config and audited.

## Anti-flap and minimum data requirements
### Minimum sample size
- Default: **>= 100 canary requests** per model tuple in the evaluation window

For models with intentionally low canary QPS, set model-specific thresholds rather than lowering the global minimum.

### Sustained windows
- Warning: **15 minutes** (rolling)
- Paging: **30 minutes** (rolling)

### Dedupe keys
Incident-bot dedupes on model + model_version, region, and regression_type (latency vs throughput).

### Recovery
Recovered when the signal is back within:
- latency: **<= +5%** of baseline for **20 minutes**
- tokens/sec: **>= -5%** of baseline for **20 minutes**

## Notification routing matrix
| Condition | Alert tier | Primary channel | Who acts | Escalation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Single model, mild regression | Warning | #eng-runtime | Runtime (business hours) | SRE if sustained > 4h or release ongoing |
| Top model sustained regression | Sev2 page | #eng-oncall + #incidents | SRE on-call + Runtime | Kernel/scheduling owners by attribution |
| Multi-model / infra-shaped | Sev2 page | #eng-oncall + #incidents | SRE on-call | Infra/Fleet (Vanessa Ortiz) + Telemetry (Logan Wright) |
| Severe widespread regression | Sev1 page | #eng-oncall + #incidents | SRE on-call + Runtime on-call | Eng leadership |

## Alert payload requirements
Each alert must carry model, version, runtime_build_id, region, hardware_sku; baseline, observed, and percent change; sample count and window; attribution hints where available; and links to the Grafana per-model dashboard, synthetic canary traces, and runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert. Missing fields are a tooling bug against telemetry/canary.

## Rollout gates
- During rollouts, **Warning alerts on gated models** need explicit acknowledgement from the release captain and runtime TL.
- **Sev2+ pages** on gated models automatically pause the rollout (Release Engineering integration) unless the incident commander overrides with a documented reason, which is only acceptable when the regression is confirmed canary-only and mitigation is underway.

## Change management and baseline integrity
Post a short note in #eng-runtime (linked from the release ticket) for: runtime build changes to scheduling/batching/kernels/memory, kernel auto-tuning updates, fleet changes (new GPU SKU, driver stack, power caps, MIG), and region capacity tier changes.

Baselines are versioned per runtime_build_id and hardware_sku, refreshed only intentionally via the baseline pipeline, and recorded in the change log. No silent rolling baselines.

## Paging hygiene
- SRE reviews paging volume weekly during rollouts; goal is **< 5 perf-canary pages/week** outside planned rollouts.
- Each paging false positive gets an incident note and a follow-up ticket (thresholds, dedupe, baseline, telemetry).
- Thresholds are revisited after major runtime releases, new top models, and fleet SKU transitions.

## Appendix A: Default thresholds
- Warning:
  - p95 latency +10% for 15m (>=100 samples)
  - tokens/sec -8% for 15m (>=100 samples)
- Sev2 (Top models):
  - p95 latency +25% for 30m
  - tokens/sec -15% for 30m
- Sev1 (Top models):
  - p95 latency +35% for 20m
  - tokens/sec -25% for 20m
